cat__gieduc_7.label: Needs caution
cat__gieduc_7.reason: Education level is a proxy for socioeconomic position and may confound associations with sleep quality through lifestyle, work schedules, and comorbidity patterns.

num__baseline_hr.label: Plausible
num__baseline_hr.reason: Higher resting heart rate can reflect sympathetic activation, poor fitness, or cardiometabolic disease, which are linked to fragmented sleep and worse perceived sleep quality.

num__gimstat.label: Needs caution
num__gimstat.reason: If this is a general health/medical status indicator, it likely captures comorbidity severity that both affects and is affected by sleep, creating confounding and potential reverse causation.

num__num_apnea_hypopnea_events.label: Plausible
num__num_apnea_hypopnea_events.reason: More apnea/hypopnea events increase sleep fragmentation and intermittent hypoxemia, which can worsen subjective sleep quality.

num__pct_n2.label: Plausible
num__pct_n2.reason: A higher proportion of N2 can reflect reduced deep sleep or altered sleep architecture, which may relate to poorer restorative sleep and lower perceived quality.

num__pct_n3.label: Plausible
num__pct_n3.reason: Lower N3 (slow-wave sleep) reduces restorative sleep and is associated with fatigue and poorer subjective sleep quality.

num__powers_c3_alpha.label: Plausible
num__powers_c3_alpha.reason: Elevated alpha power during sleep can indicate cortical arousal or lighter sleep, which may correspond to worse perceived sleep quality.

num__powers_c3_theta.label: Plausible
num__powers_c3_theta.reason: Theta power reflects sleep depth/stage composition and homeostatic sleep pressure; deviations may be associated with nonrestorative sleep.

num__powers_c4_alpha.label: Plausible
num__powers_c4_alpha.reason: Higher alpha activity during sleep is consistent with arousal/instability and may be linked to poorer subjective sleep quality.

num__powers_c4_theta.label: Plausible
num__powers_c4_theta.reason: Theta-band power relates to NREM sleep intensity and architecture; abnormal patterns can plausibly affect perceived sleep quality.

num__rem_latency_min.label: Plausible
num__rem_latency_min.reason: Altered REM latency can reflect circadian misalignment, depression, or medication effects, all of which can influence perceived sleep quality.

num__sleep_latency_min.label: Likely leakage
num__sleep_latency_min.reason: Sleep latency is a core component of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and closely overlaps the construct measured by pqpsqual.

num__spo2_mean.label: Plausible
num__spo2_mean.reason: Lower mean nocturnal oxygen saturation indicates sustained hypoxemia (often from sleep-disordered breathing), which can impair sleep continuity and perceived quality.

num__waso_min.label: Likely leakage
num__waso_min.reason: Wake after sleep onset directly measures sleep maintenance/fragmentation, which is a central component of subjective sleep quality scales like PSQI.

num__spo2_min.label: Plausible
num__spo2_min.reason: Lower minimum SpO2 reflects intermittent hypoxemia severity, which can drive arousals and nonrestorative sleep.

num__num_desats.label: Plausible
num__num_desats.reason: More oxygen desaturations indicate more frequent breathing disturbances and hypoxemic stress, plausibly worsening sleep quality via arousals and fragmentation.

num__odi4.label: Plausible
num__odi4.reason: A higher 4% oxygen desaturation index reflects more severe sleep-disordered breathing burden, which can reduce restorative sleep and perceived quality.

num__num_plm.label: Plausible
num__num_plm.reason: Periodic limb movements can cause micro-arousals and sleep fragmentation, leading to poorer subjective sleep quality.

num__powers_c4_beta.label: Plausible
num__powers_c4_beta.reason: Increased beta power during sleep can reflect hyperarousal or lighter sleep, which is often associated with insomnia symptoms and worse perceived sleep quality.

cat__gisoc_51.label: Needs caution

cat__tu12drin_1.label: Plausible
cat__tu12drin_1.reason: Alcohol use can alter sleep architecture, increase fragmentation, and worsen sleep-disordered breathing, plausibly reducing perceived sleep quality.

cat__tudramt_1.label: Plausible
cat__tudramt_1.reason: Alcohol amount is plausibly causal for poorer sleep quality via REM suppression, rebound, and increased awakenings later in the night.

cat__tudramt_2.label: Plausible
cat__tudramt_2.reason: Greater alcohol intake can worsen sleep continuity and exacerbate snoring/OSA, leading to worse subjective sleep quality.

cat__tudramt_3.label: Plausible
cat__tudramt_3.reason: Alcohol dose has a known physiological impact on sleep stages and arousal threshold, plausibly affecting perceived sleep quality.

cat__tudramt_4.label: Plausible

cat__tudramt_5.label: Plausible
cat__tudramt_5.reason: Heavy alcohol use is associated with fragmented sleep and worsened breathing disturbances, plausibly lowering perceived sleep quality.

cat__tursmoke_1.label: Plausible

cat__tusmkcgn_M.label: Plausible
cat__tusmkcgn_M.reason: Smoking status/consumption is plausibly linked to poorer sleep quality via nicotine stimulation, withdrawal overnight, and respiratory effects.

num__hrv_sdnn_ms.label: Plausible

num__hypopnea_index.label: Plausible
num__hypopnea_index.reason: More hypopneas contribute to sleep fragmentation and intermittent hypoxemia, plausibly worsening subjective sleep quality.
